title: Commercial Fusion Energy: 2026 Progress and Gaps

stats.label: US fusion deployment target
stats.detail: DOE roadmap is central federal strategy; industry says success hinges on more funding.

stats.label: Fusion funding raised in one year
stats.detail: Record worldwide in 12 months to July 2026; cumulative funding since 2021 reached $14.24B.

stats.label: ITER tokamak core now installed
stats.detail: Six of nine sector modules in the pit, almost six months ahead of schedule.

stats.label: US fusion companies
stats.detail: Most pursue tokamaks or stellarators; others use laser-based inertial confinement.

stats.label: Final ITER sector module target
stats.detail: Installation moved up from December 2027 to mid-2027.

stats.label: FES appropriation for FY2027
stats.detail: Below $805.7M enacted; 2022 law authorized up to $1.1B.

quotes.text: “The plan isn’t the problem. We all agree on the plan. The X factor is the funding.”
quotes.source: Robb Hughes, Realta Fusion, via Reuters

quotes.text: ITER is primarily an exploratory science initiative and is not designed or intended to produce electricity.
As of 2025, the National Ignition Facility is the only laboratory to have demonstrated a fusion energy gain factor above one.
“With six modules now in place, we are demonstrating that this technical approach is delivering tangible results on the project’s critical path.”

takeaway: Fusion’s 2030s targets are real, but funding and engineering—tritium, materials, and net gain—remain the gatekeepers.
